chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Canada dates with no publicity or billing
summary: After about four weeks of the show they played two weeks in Canada on a bill with Lilly St. Clair where Nazarro's manager never sent publicity.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So after we finished the show we did -- I guess we did about four weeks of that show, then we went to Canada.
Were you doing your routine in this show?
Yeah, I did the routine, dancing, singing, piano playing.
Your standard routine?
Yeah, standard
routine, mh-hm.
So what happened in Canada?
Well, we got work to do our act up there.
Nazarro was booking this --

Yeah, he booked us there, but he wasn't working in the act. So he booked us up there to work on his program. He didn't give no publicity for the man to give us any billing so we found that Lilly St. Clair was playing on the bill and couldn't find our name out there nowhere. Finally he told us the manager didn't send no publicity on us, so he couldn't put nothing out. So we told him what we could and we worked two weeks up there and we were coming back to New York.
Who were you working with up there?
No other group, There was about eight acts on the bill, I don't
know the name of the acts but I know that St. Clair was one of them that was headlining. I think we split the billing with her.
Now this was prior to your major Broadway career of Blackbirds, Porgy & Bess --
Yeah. Yeah.
Prior to that major Hollywood films that you had done, "One for the Show," "Cabin in the Sky." Right.
No, we didn't get the offer of the show yet.
You hadn't gotten it.
No. I got to come back to that, because that happened in 1937.
And this is about what year?
They bought the show in 1937.
